which_binary_has_the_behavioural_change: The frozen oracle predates MD-12 and is behaviourally stock MAME plus observation hooks only. The stunrun-observe build at /mnt/build/mame-ref/mame includes the MD-12 fix, so it is NOT a behavioural substitute for the oracle: a measurement taken with it must be recorded as such, and must not be compared against anything in reference/ that was captured with the frozen oracle.

MD-12 triage. internal_regs_map exposes offsets 0x00-0x1ff while m_IOregs holds 64 entries and IOREG() indexes it unmasked. Prints sizeof(m_IOregs), the byte delta to m_shiftreg, and where each out-of-bounds offset actually lands, rather than inferring it from the class layout.
patches.added: 2026-10-14, authored outside this session; recorded by tests/test_mame_local_patches.py, which failed on it as designed

patches.purpose: Count 68010 accesses to one address window, histogrammed by the issuing PC. Lua memory taps do not fire on this 68010 in this build -- install_read_tap and install_write_tap both report zero over ranges the same arm touches heavily (0x00C00000, 780,315 writes natively) -- so no Lua tap result is usable and the C++ passthrough tap is required. First job, settled: the watchdog window 0x608000-0x60bfff gave MAME 1263 against native's 1259 over 320 frames, the same cadence on both, which withdrew findings 110.2's 36-frame edge as boundary sampling phase. Second job: the ADSP service-test strings at 0x6df1-0x6ea4 are reached by no 32-bit pointer that a text search can find (only 7 of 203 string starts in 0x6b00-0x8700 are pointer targets at all), so the read direction records which PC actually touches them instead. Passthrough tap, so the underlying handler still runs; observation-only, armed only when STUNRUN_CPU_WCOUNT_START is set. Histogram prints once at exit. See findings section 115 and 117.
patches.env_note: STUNRUN_CPU_WCOUNT_BYPC is an output prefix, not a switch: the guard test inventories every STUNRUN_ token in the diff as an environment variable, so it is recorded here rather than left to look like an unrecorded control.

behaviour_changes.reason: The MD-12 memory-safety fix. m_IOregs grew from 64 to 0x200 entries and IOREG() now masks its offset to 0x1ff (and SMART_IOREG routes through IOREG). CORRECTED 2026-10-17: an earlier version of this reason claimed 'this game's GSP program writes at 0x90-0x160, so this changes the oracle's behaviour'. THAT CLAIM IS WRONG. Measured on md12-fixed (which contains the STUNRUN_GSP_IOBREPORT hook, unlike the frozen oracle): 600 frames power-on and 600 frames of service mode produced NO write at MAME-offset >= 0x40 -- the report file is fopen'ed inside the offset>=64 branch, so its absence is positive evidence the branch was never taken. Findings 52.2 (same conclusion, but VACUOUS: the oracle lacks the hook) and 86.2 (the non-vacuous re-run). So the fix is INERT for S.T.U.N. Runner: the two binaries behave identically on these paths and this patch is not why their frame-600 output differs. The fix stays because the overflow is real in the unfixed array.

provenance_note: STUNRUN-IOB appeared in the MAME working tree while this session was running and was not authored here. It is recorded because an unrecorded hook in the oracle is exactly the failure tests/test_mame_local_patches.py exists to catch. Its observation-only status was read off its body, not assumed. The MD-12 fix is filed under behaviour_changes rather than patches for the same reason: the guard rejects any non-observation-only entry in patches, and calling this one observation-only would be false. Note that tms34010.h now appears in BOTH lists -- it carries observation hooks and a behavioural fix inside one diff, which is exactly the case the file-level check cannot detect on its own.
